why: cheat sheet people bookmark and reuse every season
posts:
The most common mistake in amateur sport is picking a format that does not match your entry count.

Straight knockout with 20 teams means 10 of them drive home after 20 minutes of football.

What to run at each size:

Up to 6 teams → single round robin.

5 rounds, 15 matches, one day. Everyone plays everyone, nobody is eliminated.

At youth level that matters more than drama. The kid came to play, not to watch.

8–16 teams → groups plus knockout.

4 groups, 24 group matches, 7 knockout matches, two days.

Every team is guaranteed at least three games and you still get a real bracket with a final. The best balance for inter-school championships.

More than 16 teams → Swiss system.

32 teams, 5 rounds, nobody eliminated. Opponents are matched on current points, so weak teams avoid hammerings and strong teams avoid free wins.

Special case: 4–8 teams but you want a proper showpiece final.

Double elimination. One defeat does not end you — you drop to the lower bracket and can still reach the final from there.

Borrowed from esports, almost unheard of in grassroots sport.

Always avoid:

— Round robin with 16 teams in one day. That is 120 matches.
— Groups of six across two days. You will not finish the group stage.
— Straight knockout when teams have travelled far.

How many teams do you usually get?

Drop the number and I will tell you which format I would run and why.
